simple.meaning: סְנַפִּיר (çᵉnappîyr) is a Hebrew action word meaning “a fin (collectively).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 5 times in Leviticus, Deuteronomy, beginning at Leviticus 11:9. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to סְנַפִּיר (H5579) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: סְנַפִּיר (çᵉnappîyr) / H5579 is traced through Leviticus 11:9, Leviticus 11:10, Leviticus 11:12, Deuteronomy 14:9 with source-language evidence and verse context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: “ ‘These you may eat of all that are in the waters: whatever has fins and scales in the waters, in the seas, and in the rivers, that you may eat.

timeline.evidenceText: “ ‘These you may eat of all that are in the waters: whatever has fins and scales in the waters, in the seas, and in the rivers, that you may eat.
All that don’t have fins and scales in the seas and rivers, all that move in the waters, and all the living creatures that are in the waters, they are an abomination to you,
Whatever has no fins nor scales in the waters is an abomination to you.
These you may eat of all that are in the waters: you may eat whatever has fins and scales.
You shall not eat whatever doesn’t have fins and scales. It is unclean to you.

definitions.full: H5579. senappir סְנַמִּיר noun [masculine] fin (Late Hebrew id. ; quadriliteral according to Sta § 243 ; Fl in Levy NHWB iii. 725 a compare Aramaic סִמְמּוֺרִין points, nails , and derive this from סַמֵּר verb nail , with infixed פ (Levy ChWB ii. 507 b )); — Lev 11:9-10 , 12 = Deut 14:9-10 ,.
